To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ALSFRS-R ratio within the first 100 days is the most powerful predictor for survival in ALS patients.
the ALSFRS-R ratio is an independent predictor for survival in ALS.
the ratio of change in ALSFRS-R within 100 days of disease onset is a useful prognostic factor in ALS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of factors that predict ALS survival.
the identification and evaluation of predictors of survival in ALS.
the development of a prognostic score to predict survival in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratio of the ALSFRS-R scores at symptom onset and at first visit, during whole disease and within 100 days are useful predictors of survival in a large cohort of ALS-patients.
a ratio of 1.0 or more is associated with longer survival time.
the ratio of the ALSFRS-R within 100 days after the first symptom is a useful prognostic factor in ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALSFRS-R ratio within 100 days after first symptom is a good predictor for survival.
the ratio of change of the ALSFRS-R within 100 days of disease duration is a useful parameter in clinical trials as well as in daily clinical work.
the ratio of the ALSFRS-R between first symptom and the first examination, during the whole disease or within the first 100 days is an independent and useful prognostic factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of the ALSFRS-R between the first symptom and the time of first examination is a good indicator of survival.
the ALSFRS-R ratio within 100 days after diagnosis is a useful parameter in daily clinical practice and clinical trials.
the ratio of the ALSFRS-R scores at the first symptom and at the first visit, as well as the ratio of the first visit and 100 days, are useful predictors for the survival time in ALS patients.
